newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Two Russian cosmonauts begin space walk.
newsitem.headline: Two Russian cosmonauts begin space walk.

text.p: Two Russian cosmonauts from the Mir orbiting station, Valery Korzun and Alexander Koleri, began a six-hour space walk on Monday, a spokesman at the mission control centre said.
"The cosmonauts opened a hatch at 6.54 p.m. (0354 GMT) and began work outside the station," the spokesman told Reuters by telephone.
He said U.S. astronaut John Blaha stayed inside the Mir to observe and monitor his colleagues' operations.
The spokesman said that during the space walk the cosmonauts would connect the second section of a U.S.-made solar panel to provide power for the Mir.
"The first section was connected earlier, but it could only provide a partial power supply," he said.
The solar panel was delivered to Mir by the U.S Atlantis space shuttle last year.

"If today's space walk is successful the Mir will have a 100 percent power supply," the spokesman said, adding that the cosmonauts' work would be complicated. "It consists of many difficult operations," he said.
Blaha and his two Russian colleagues have been in orbit on Mir since September 19.
